trust_decision.summary: The query builder decides whether a filter value counts as numeric (from DataType 'number' or a propertyKeyMap entry) and then writes it into the ClickHouse SQL string unquoted and unchecked; string values are quoted and escaped. Decided in charts.addFilter/buildCond in backend/pkg/analytics/charts/query.go.

landing_point.why: The advisory names session search. The handler for POST /{projectId}/sessions/search reaches charts.BuildWhere here, and one hop on is query.go, where every fix site sits.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /{projectId}/sessions/search (and /sessions/search/ids, /cards/try) with a numeric filter and operator isNot or not plus several values
POST /{projectId}/sessions/search with a numeric filter and operator is, =, <, >, <= or >= (through multiValCond, or formatCondition for a single isNot)
public Go API charts.BuildWhere/BuildEventConditions with operator in/notIn and one value; the HTTP validator's operator oneof list does not include in or notIn
public Go API charts.BuildWhere with operator in/notIn and several values (same validator note)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: backend/pkg/analytics/saved_searches/saved_searches.go:276-286 (stored saved-search filters are sent through search.GetCounts to charts.BuildWhere at backend/pkg/analytics/search/search.go:508); also stored segment filters are expanded into the live request at backend/pkg/analytics/lexicon/resolver.go:138-144

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Saved-search stats and segment expansion are a neighbouring feature that replays filters already saved in Postgres rather than a 'search request', so a solver who adds request validation (for example a numeric validator tag on Filter.Value for /sessions/search) can argue that stored filters are out of scope. The published fix closes them only because it sits at the shared sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate numeric filters (status code 404, tag_id, negatives such as -5, floats such as 3.14) must still render unquoted, so that comparisons against JSONExtractFloat(...) keep working. An over-broad fix that quotes every value as a string, or rejects the whole filter, breaks numeric comparisons. String values must stay quoted and escaped, and the valueless isAny/isUndefined operators must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: single value through formatCondition (is, =, <, >, <=, >=, single isNot)
several values combined with OR through multiValCond
several values in a NOT IN list (isNot/not branch of buildCond)
values with surrounding whitespace (the fix applies TrimSpace before ParseFloat)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second numeric session-column builder (for example screen_width/screen_height or a duration-like range filter) that formats the value with %s instead of ParseInt/%d
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BuildDurationWhere already special-cases one numeric session column, and SessionColumns lists screen_width/screen_height (query.go:851-852). A maintainer adding a range filter for these by copying the pattern could easily skip the ParseInt.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a numeric exclusion/start-point condition in the journey builder that writes ef.Value directly into its own Sprintf instead of going through buildCond
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This builder already assembles its own condition strings by hand next to BuildEventConditions, so a hand-rolled numeric branch here would sit in another file and bypass the fixed helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a breakdown-specific numeric bucket condition (status code ranges) built outside buildCond
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Breakdowns already include statusCode (model.go:92), and a range bucket written next to the breakdown code is a plausible second implementation at a distance.

O10_build.project_tests: backend/pkg/analytics/charts/query_test.go and breakdown_test.go exercise the string-building helpers without a database. The fix adds backend/pkg/analytics/charts/query_sqli_test.go (absent at the pinned commit), which calls BuildWhere directly. ClickHouse is needed only to execute queries, not to test SQL generation.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Patch only formatCondition (the single-value '=' path the report reproduces), or add a request validator tag on Filter.Value, which leaves the isNot multi-value list, inClause, and stored saved-search/segment filters open.

out_of_scope_notes: backend/pkg/analytics/charts/query.go:281-282 and backend/pkg/analytics/charts/metric_table.go:677-678 pass a metadata_-prefixed f.Name as the raw SQL expression (identifier position, not covered by the numeric-value fix).
backend/pkg/analytics/charts/metric_user_journey.go:259 and :274 write ef.Name / MetricValue into a quoted literal without sqlStringReplacer.
backend/pkg/analytics/charts/metric_heatmaps_session.go:183 writes the url_path filter value into '%s' without escaping.
The Python chalice session search (api/chalicelib/core/sessions/sessions_ch.py:73) binds values as %(key)s parameters; json_key is interpolated at :63/:68 (not checked further).
unverified: repo_mb: not measured (no shell); openreplay is a multi-component monorepo, probably well above 5 MB.

O1 counts POST /sessions/search, /sessions/search/ids, /cards/try, /cards/{id}/try, /cards/{id}/chart and the saved-search list/get stats path. The card routes go through charts.go:59 NewQueryBuilder; I did not trace every metric type to BuildWhere. /cards/{id}/sessions was not traced.
Whether the card endpoints run validator.Struct on MetricPayload (which would also block in/notIn there) was not checked; inClause looks reachable only through the public Go API or stored filters.
Whether saved searches/segments can hold values that the request path would reject was not checked beyond model.go:221 (dive validation at save time; no numeric check on Value).

sqlNumericLiteral accepts anything strconv.ParseFloat accepts (Inf, NaN, hex floats such as 0x1p3, underscores); I did not check whether all of these are valid ClickHouse literals. This is not an injection, but it may matter for hidden-test fairness.
